artworks.title: Heracles Feasting in the House of Eurytus
artworks.description: Corinthian column-krater (Louvre E635): Heracles banquets in Eurytus of Oechalia’s hall — the household of Iphitus before friendship soured into the murder that sent Heracles to Omphale. Archaic vase-painting keeps Eurytus’ sons, including Iphitus, in the visual prelude to the bow-gift Odyssey later remembers.

popCulture.title: Odyssey XXI (Iphitus’ bow)
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer’s digression: Iphitus son of Eurytus gave Odysseus his father’s bow in Messene — the weapon of the suitors’ contest — before Heracles slew the guest-friend.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca (Heracles and Iphitus)
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus tells how Heracles threw Iphitus from the Tirynthian walls in a fit of madness — the crime that sold the hero into Omphale’s service.
